title: Pattern enum → PatternOp trait — ops own names, no central variant match
description:
Current v3 has Pattern as a central enum (Regex/Glob/Json/Ast) with Pattern::as_raw_regex, Pattern::bound_captures, Pattern::apply, Pattern::materialize_for all dispatching via match-self. This violates the ops-own-everything invariant (§14.1, feedback_op_owns_everything). Migrate to:

- Pattern becomes a trait (renamed to PatternValue or folded into the existing PatternOp with a cursor-value face).
- Value::Pattern holds Arc<dyn PatternValue> (or Arc<dyn PatternOp>).
- Each pattern op impls trait methods: as_raw_regex, bound_captures, apply, materialize_for.
- All match-on-Pattern-variant sites flip to dyn trait calls.

Blocks sprefa-4m7.14 landing in its locked form. Without this, the "pattern op instance passed as arg" question devolves back to central dispatch.

- v3/crates/pipeline/src/value.rs (the enum itself)

- anywhere else grep finds Pattern::Regex / Pattern::Glob / match on Pattern

title: SPIKE: keyed wait-set runtime primitive — unifies park, tag re-entry, lazy parametric rules, xref semijoin
description:
Synthesis spike: a single runtime primitive (a keyed wait-set on the runtime) collapses four separately-described mechanics into one shape:

1. §19.2 cursor park on missing term — "term missing, upstream emitting → cursor parks (backpressure)". Currently spec-locked, no implementation; no shape for what holds the cursor during the park.

2. Tag op re-entry / xref semijoin — unbound-mode `tag($X, :kind)` reading the tag store should fan out one cursor per existing row AND remain subscribed so a later write of the same kind retroactively wakes parked readers. Today the tag-op contract (§24.2 / project_v3_tag_op_prolog_posture) describes synchronous read/write against an in-memory HashMap; no reactivity wire.

3. Parametric rule with unbound captures (sprefa-4m7.5.6) — "sprefa's function-def mechanism". Rule body is a subscribed continuation parked on its unbound params until a call site supplies them. The same wake mechanic.

4. Scan-pointer Tri verification (memory: project_scan_pointer_runtime) — content-side captures stamped `Claimed` flip to `Verified` once a command-side `repo($R)` writes a matching value. The flip is a delayed wake on the capture's identity. Same mechanic at the capture layer.

The unifying primitive: `WaitKey` discriminator over { Term(name), Tag(kind, value), TagAny(kind), Capture(path, value) }. A cursor parks against one or more WaitKeys; any op that writes a binding under those keys fires the wake. xref-callers = subscribe with a wildcard discriminator.

This is what 'opt-in to pausing and waiting' actually means at the runtime layer.
notes:
**Reading list**
- parse.md §19.2 (2326-2335) — runtime wait semantics, locked but unimplemented
- parse.md §21 (2375-2392) — SubscribePolicy::{Cold, Shared{store_key}, Memo} — Subject-shaped store key is the candidate WaitKey
- parse.md §22 (2396-2415) — mergeByKey runtime; key = (rule_path, term_path); maps cleanly onto WaitKey
- parse.md §24.1 (2456-2467) — relations schema; tag store reads/writes flow here
- parse.md §24.2 (2470-2480) — tag-op family contract
- parse.md §14.5m.3 (1733-1759) — three op shapes; produce-or-filter is the row-emitter side of the wake protocol
- memory: project_v3_tag_op_prolog_posture — bidirectional tag, [Either, BoundOnly], in-memory tag store
- memory: project_scan_pointer_runtime — Tri verification (Claimed/Verified/Missing) is the capture-layer instance of the same mechanic
- memory: project_no_ans_ref — scan-pointer is a regular op reading cursor.last_bound; supersedes $$ sigil
- bd: sprefa-4m7.5.6 — N-arity unbound-captures = lazy rule def; resolver representation of 'rule waiting for N slots'
- bd: sprefa-4m7.7.2 — tag-op family contract
- bd: sprefa-4m7.2.14 — tag op family — bidirectional prolog-style relation
- bd: sprefa-4m7.7.9 — paused/blocked runtime visualization (downstream consumer of this primitive)
- bd: sprefa-4m7.6.1 — fork capture intersection (interacts: a parked cursor in one arm shouldn't deadlock the meet)

**Concrete questions for the spike**

1. WaitKey discriminator — what shapes are needed?
   - Term(name) — cursor parks waiting for any op to bind $name on it
   - Tag(kind, value) — exact-match wait (tag value already known, waiting for the row to land)
   - TagAny(kind) — wildcard, the xref-callers shape: 'wake me on every row of this kind'
   - Capture(path, value) — Tri-verification flip
   - RuleParam(rule_id, param_idx) — parametric rule waiting on caller supply
   The four cases may collapse: (Tag, TagAny, Capture) all key on (kind/path, optional value).

2. Park handle — what physically holds the cursor during the park?
   - Candidate A: per-key tokio::sync::Notify; cursor task awaits notify.notified().
   - Candidate B: bounded mpsc per WaitKey; writer sends, parked task receives.
   - Candidate C: WaitSet<WaitKey> on runtime, indexed; writer fires fire(key) → wake all subscribers.
   - Backpressure semantics differ: A wakes all (broadcast), B is fan-out fan-in, C is up to indexer.

3. Subscription lifetime — when does a parked subscription drop?
   - Upstream-closed (per §19.2): drop the cursor.
   - Cancellation (per §22 unsubscribe): drop.
   - Shared SubscribePolicy: stays alive across multiple subscribers via store_key.
   - Cold: per-subscribe park; new subscribe gets fresh wait.

4. Re-entry vs replay — does an unbound tag($X, :kind) read see rows written *before* the read?
   - BehaviorSubject mapping (§22) implies yes: subscribe → replay all current rows + subscribe to future.
   - This is the xref semijoin shape: query-time + reactive subscription to future writes.

5. Static analysis — can the resolver detect unsatisfiable waits at lower time?
   - For rules: yes, via BindingGraph (§19.1). Already designed.
   - For tags: harder; only known at runtime. May need a 'will-write' annotation on tag ops to enable lower-time detection.

6. Interaction with fork intersection (§20.1) — if a cursor in arm A parks on $X and arm B doesn't bind $X, does the fork merge wait or proceed?
   - Probably proceed-without-arm-A; the meet of $X is empty so downstream can't reference it anyway.

7. Implementation seam — where does the wait-set live?
   - effect_runtime crate as a new primitive alongside Batcher?
   - pipeline crate as part of the runner?
   - Cleanest: effect_runtime, since 'park / wake on key' is a runtime-shape concern, not pipeline-specific.

**What this unlocks**

- xref query primitive (`tags(:kind, $X)` with unbound $X) — fan out current rows + subscribe to future writes
- Lazy parametric rules — rule body becomes a subscription parked on RuleParam wait keys
- Retroactive scan-pointer verification — content-side Claimed captures flip to Verified when command-side writes land
- Reactive tag-store updates — a `tag` write fires wakes for all parked readers of that kind
- §19.2 implementation — the park primitive that the spec already promised

**What stays pure**

- Op trait surface unchanged. Wait/wake is a runtime mechanic, ops just write captures.
- Resolver static analysis (BindingGraph, ArgSpec, derived rule mode) unchanged.
- §22 mergeByKey runtime model already uses keyed events; this is the keyed-wait dual.

**Out of scope for the spike**

- SQLite persistence of tag store (covered by sprefa-4m7.7.6)
- LSP visualization of paused cursors (covered by sprefa-4m7.7.9)
- Cross-process / cross-machine wait keys (single-process for now)

title: Carveouts inside pattern bodies — Seg::Computed + per-op template materialization
description:
A carveout_expr (${...}) inside a pattern sub-grammar body is a runtime-computed splice. Needs:

- Extend per-op Seg enum with Computed { pipe: Arc<Pipeline> }.
- Extend each pattern sub-grammar (re, glob, json, ast, cst) to recognize carveout_expr as a body child. §14.3 shared-fragment needs carveout_expr lifted into the shared set.

title: SPIKE: Pattern IS Op — unify pattern/pipeline/tuple/struct under single trait
description:
Patterns, pipelines, tuples, and structs all share the shape 'list-of-cursors -> list-of-cursors'. If Pattern::compile returns Arc<dyn Op>, Value collapses to a single Op variant (plus Tuple if a const-shape concession is kept). Bulk-path specialization (e.g. fs driving a compiled regex in batch) becomes Any-downcast at the outer op's discretion, not a separate Value variant.

Thesis artifacts:
- tuple (A, B, C) = Seq[A, B, C] = A > B > C (pipe) at the AST level
- struct { f: v, g: w } = Seq[set(f, v), set(g, w)] emitting a record cursor (allocation-over-time)
- $TERM = term(X) op = identity-with-capture-bind
- patterns with unbound terms = ops with non-empty free-variable set; evaluating requires a body (why rev($V) is rejected: term-only into filter semantic has nothing to bind from)

Tradeoffs to explore:
- Op trait object-safety vs bulk-path specialization via Any (already the current posture, §14.2b)
- Registry factory signature: does it still need Vec<Value> or does a single Arc<dyn Op> per slot suffice? (probably still tuple for n-ary)
- Do we keep Pattern as a named concept at all, or does it evaporate into 'Op with the PatternOp extension trait'?

Relation to 14: 14 lands the Value enum and nested op_invocation in slots. This spike asks whether Value should start with 4 variants or 1. Likely direction: land 14 with Value having Pattern/Pipeline separate, then this spike proposes the collapse as a follow-up so 14 is not blocked on the trait redesign.
notes:
## 2026-04-22 landed — Pass A: Value collapse + PatternValue deletion + consumer migration

### What shipped

Concrete matchers (GlobPattern, RegexPattern, JsonPattern, AstPattern, AstStructuralConfirm) deleted — fields fused into GlobOp/ReOp directly. Placeholder Json/Ast patterns removed (uncallable until those ops land).
- ArgSpec collapsed: Pattern + Pipeline variants replaced by single Op.
- GlobOp/ReOp (ops/glob, ops/re) rewritten: hold template/regex/bound_captures/anchors directly. Static compile_from_tree returns Self. Op::pipe runs apply_identity_pattern directly. Op::try_raw_regex/materialize_with/bound_captures override capability defaults. Macro-based #[sprf_pattern_op] removed from these two — manual impl Op block is cleaner than extending the macro for capability delegation.
- PatternOp trait (pattern_op.rs) slimmed: kept binds_captures (tree-walk probe) and hover_match. Dropped compile, compiled_pattern, pattern_pipe default. Pattern ops now construct via inherent compile_from_tree (Self: Sized, so outside the dyn-safe trait).
- Consumers (fs/rev/repo/comment): stopped downcasting Value::Pattern(Arc<dyn PatternValue>) to &GlobPattern/&RegexPattern. New match arm: Value::Op(op) if op.try_raw_regex().is_some(). RevOp/RepoOp/FsOp now hold Arc<dyn Op> in their Filter variants; pipe time calls op.try_raw_regex().is_match(...). CommentOp pulls the regex via op.try_raw_regex().unwrap().clone().

title: Rule auto-schema: captures as wide table, streaming INSERT sink
description: Each cursor emitted by a rule is a row in the rule's auto-created table. Wide layout: columns = union of binds_captures() across the rule's pipeline, plus {repo, rev, fs}. Per-capture columns: name is the capture name prefix, with suffixes _lo and _hi (byte range). Synthesized captures get an additional _value TEXT column since they have no span. Schema computed at lower time from static traversal of the pipeline (PatternOp::binds_captures reports, > $NAME capture-write declares, Synthesized producers declare). Terminal sink is an implicit sql_write into the auto-schema'd table unless the rule body overrides. Rule knows its cursors via SprfPath prefix match. Relations-tier streaming means no in-RAM accumulator, no arena pressure: the table is the arena.

**CST capture-sigil rule**
tree-sitter native @name is not sprf-legal; cst sub-grammar requires @$A or @${A} in authored source. Compile renders @$A to @A when emitting tree-sitter Query source; captured nodes map 1:1 to sprf captures on output cursor. value: sprefa positioning vs graph-topology runtimes (Airflow/Celery/Temporal/Prefect/Dagster/Flink/Timely/Materialize). Overlap with each on one axis, distinct on three: (1) ops are code-analysis-shaped (glob/re/ast/fs/repo/rev/cursor-narrowing), not generic tasks; (2) pattern-arg composition is the reuse unit - pipelines are values the outer op drives - Airflow/Celery cannot introspect task body; (3) lowers to Rust byte loops (ast-grep/biome tier), not Airflow/Prefect tier. Durable-workflow-replay (Temporal) is the one property that would force a language-level decision; skipped for now, rely on relations tier idempotence on rerun. v0/v1/v2 strings+refs indexing table reduces to a ~15-line .sprf recipe in v3 using fs(glob) > ast[lang](string_literal > $S) > sql_write. Core holds no opinion about what an index is.

Value/Pattern/ArgSpec type surface landed in v3/crates/pipeline/src/value.rs but NOT wired: (1) lower.rs never constructs Value::Pattern from nested re/glob invocations -- fs/repo/rev don't receive Value; (2) Op::arg_spec() declared but not consulted by lowerer; (3) lower::ArgSpec{accepts:AcceptsMode} and value::ArgSpec enum share a name, unrelated concerns, no bridge; (4) Value::Pipeline and Value::Atom unconsumed; (5) Pattern::Json and Pattern::Ast variants declared, no op emits them. re/glob compile to Pattern and OnceLock-stash it; default pattern_pipe drives Pattern::apply. str stays constant, no holes.

cst op capture sigil rule (2026-04-22): cst[$LANG] body must use @$A or @${A} for captures, never bare @A. Rationale: sprefa's term grammar is the only source of truth for captures. Compile strips leading $ / ${} when rendering actual tree-sitter Query source, so tree-sitter's Query parser sees @A. Output cursor captures are named $A / ${A} per sprf conventions. Sub-grammar: _term_ref = '@' ('$' IDENT | '${' IDENT '}'). Filed on card 2.28.

Design closures locked 2026-04-22: (1) scan-pointer redundant — $A > norm in arg slot lowers to Value::Pipeline, collapses §12 and cursor.last_bound into sub-pipeline-as-argument; filed 4.11. (2) Cursor-as-wide-row: each cursor emitted by a rule is one SQLite row; columns = {repo,rev,fs} + per-capture {name_lo, name_hi} with optional _value for Synthesized; schema static at lower time from binds_captures() union; filed 7.11. (3) Arenas unnecessary: streaming INSERT flushes rows as they arrive, rules don't accumulate, relations tier IS the arena; SOA-cursor-batches are a perf lever when measured, not an architectural requirement. (4) Rule-owns-cursor via SprfPath prefix match; terminal sink is implicit sql_write into rule's auto-schema'd table.

2026-04-22 landed: sprefa-4m7.14 + sprefa-q5a. Full 3-layer trait model live: Op (base) -> PatternOp (compile-time sub-trait on op structs) + PatternValue (run-time trait on matcher structs, Pattern = Arc<dyn PatternValue>). fs/repo/rev/comment migrated to from_values(Vec<Value>); registry.build takes Vec<Value>; lower_paren_slot in registry.rs walks paren_slot children dispatching by node kind. rev($V) rejected with rev/unbounded-capture; :atom sugar flows as Value::Atom; bare ident diagnosed as value/bare-ident. 95 tests green across pipeline+sprefa_parse. Still open: sprefa-dkm (Seg::Computed carveouts in patterns), sprefa-aw5 (side-effect-only splice collapse), sprefa-x5b (Pattern IS Op full unification), sprefa-qoy (line op port), sprefa-4m7.4.9 (ArgSpec name collision hygiene), sprefa-4m7.11.2 (backend.rs audit).

ghcacher-as-sprf recipe: minimum new op set to recreate ~/projects/ghcacher in .sprf is http(+cache reader), sql_query, sql_write, interval, throttle/debounce/take/repeat, filter, fanout/on, sh[]. Ten thin effect-adapter ops. Relations tier (§24) + arg-mode read replaces scan for durable state; scan-pointer (§12) covers narrower pass-forward case. Every accumulator becomes a relation write + a rule reading it back. ghcacher's call_log/change_log/poll_state tables exemplify the pattern. Pure-rxjs-without-scan generalizes: runtime keeps no hidden slot, state is reified as rows, joins replace folds. Lowering posture matches ast-grep/biome: sprf composes ops that are already Rust impls of pipe; nothing exits Rust perf territory at the op boundary.

2026-04-22 locked for sprefa-4m7.14: nested op_invocation in paren_slot grammar LANDED; :atom sugar for scalar filters; rev($V) rejected with rev/unbounded-capture diagnostic (rev(re($V)) is the explicit opt-in); factory signature flips from (name,body_src) to (name,Vec<Value>); companion cards sprefa-q5a (enum->trait), sprefa-x5b (Pattern IS Op), sprefa-dkm (Seg::Computed for carveouts in patterns), sprefa-aw5 (side-effect-only splice collapse), sprefa-qoy (line op port). 4.7 and 4.8 subsumed by 14.

ast vs cst op split (2026-04-22): tree-sitter grammar dispatch is build-time, so dynamic grammar picks inside a bracket slot are impossible. Factoring: ast[$LANG](...) takes ast-grep pattern-by-example syntax (sweet spot: code-shaped patterns like TODO($ISSUE)); cst[$LANG](...) takes tree-sitter query S-expressions (sweet spot: structural one-liners like (string_literal) @S). Both compile to Value::Pattern(Pattern::Ast) with different confirm strategies. Sub-grammar inside each is lang-agnostic at source, lang-resolved at pattern-compile via tree-sitter language blob load. CST is the accurate name: tree-sitter produces a lossless CST, ast-grep is a pattern-by-example layer on top. Strings indexer recipe uses cst[$LANG]((string_literal) @S) as the cleaner form; ast[$LANG] is the form for content-shaped matches. Filed 2.28.

Capture-sigil form per sub-grammar (locked 2026-04-22). cst body requires @${NAME} only; ast body requires ${NAME} only. Bare $NAME illegal in both because their token alphabets abut identifier chars and ambiguate. re, glob, host accept both $NAME and ${NAME}. v2's ${VAR} sugar for ast-grep was the precedent; v3 promotes it to mandatory. Filed on 2.11 (ast) and 2.28 (cst).

Pattern-op position duality + nestable ast/cst (locked 2026-04-22, parse.md §14.2b §14.2c): same PatternOp::compile produces Pattern value used in two ways. At pipe-step it drives Op::pipe -> Pattern::apply. At arg slot it is Value::Pattern the outer op introspects. Choice lives entirely in host lowerer via outer op's ArgSpec. Nested ast/cst: second structural op re-parses the narrowed cursor.content[byte_range] per §14.5b content contract; same mechanic as any pipe-step chain. Brace-block sugar 'ast(outer){ > ast(inner); > ... }' desugars to linear chain; exists for readability. Pattern ops carry no special status in the pipe - they emit cursors, downstream consumes.

Unification thesis 2026-04-22: Pattern IS Op. list-of-cursors -> list-of-cursors is the universal shape. Tuple (A,B,C) == Seq == A>B>C pipe at AST level. Struct {f:v,g:w} == Seq of field-set ops (allocation-over-time). $TERM == term(X) op == identity-with-bind. rev($V) rejection is semantic (filter has nothing to bind from), not type-level. Tracked as sprefa-x5b spike. Still pending: does Value collapse fully to Arc<dyn Op> or keep 4 variants; decided to ship sprefa-4m7.14 with 4-variant Value and land the collapse as follow-up.
